result.regime_text: Buoyancy dominates, as on Earth, but the induced flow is weaker, so flames are taller and slower than in 1 g.
result.fan_shutdown_effect: limited: buoyancy alone still drives about 0.57 m/s of flow toward the flame

data.text: Buoyant flow is about 0.575 m/s against 1.415 m/s on Earth, so fan-to-buoyancy ratio is 0.17: buoyant regime. Buoyancy dominates, as on Earth, but the induced flow is weaker, so flames are taller and slower than in 1 g. Relevance of the normal-gravity upward-burning screening test: high.

sections.title: Evidence base
bullets: 23 combustion investigations from NASA PSI (18 flight, 5 ground).
2 non-combustion record(s) removed; 0 partial-gravity investigations exist.

sections.title: Mission
bullets: Lunar surface habitat: 0.165 g, 8.2 psia, 34% O2, fan 0.1 m/s.
Scenario assumption: 8.2 psia / 34% O2, a NASA-considered exploration atmosphere (PSI-20).

sections.title: Flame regime
bullets: Buoyant flow is about 0.575 m/s against 1.415 m/s on Earth, so fan-to-buoyancy ratio is 0.17: buoyant regime. Buoyancy dominates, as on Earth, but the induced flow is weaker, so flames are taller and slower than in 1 g. Relevance of the normal-gravity upward-burning screening test: high.
Fan shutdown effect: limited: buoyancy alone still drives about 0.57 m/s of flow toward the flame.

recommendations.text: Check heater, fan and switch ratings against every power source used on the ground and in flight.

recommendations.title: Treat oxygen generators as ignition hazards
recommendations.text: Inspect canisters for contamination, activate them away from escape routes, and keep the path to the return vehicle clear.

report.headline: Lunar surface habitat: 8 of 10 cabin materials burn or could burn at 34% O2; none of those claims rests on a NASA test at these conditions.

sections.title: Evidence base
bullets: 23 combustion investigations from NASA PSI (18 flight, 5 ground).
2 non-combustion record(s) removed; 0 partial-gravity investigations exist.

sections.title: Mission
bullets: Lunar surface habitat: 0.165 g, 8.2 psia, 34% O2, fan 0.1 m/s.
Scenario assumption: 8.2 psia / 34% O2, a NASA-considered exploration atmosphere (PSI-20).

sections.title: Flame regime
bullets: Buoyant flow is about 0.575 m/s against 1.415 m/s on Earth, so fan-to-buoyancy ratio is 0.17: buoyant regime. Buoyancy dominates, as on Earth, but the induced flow is weaker, so flames are taller and slower than in 1 g. Relevance of the normal-gravity upward-burning screening test: high.
Fan shutdown effect: limited: buoyancy alone still drives about 0.57 m/s of flow toward the flame.

sections.title: Material risk
bullets: Cotton fabric: burns (margin +14.2 +/- 4 pts, no data)
Nomex (aramid): burns (margin +3.7 +/- 4 pts, no data)
Nylon (hook-and-loop): burns (margin +8.7 +/- 4 pts, no data)
Paper / cellulose: burns (margin +14.7 +/- 4 pts, no data)
PMMA (acrylic): burns (margin +15.2 +/- 4 pts, no data)
Skeptic approved the final ranking.

sections.title: Lessons from past fires
bullets: Apollo 1 (1967): high match. Oxygen-enriched cabin (34% O2); Soft goods that can burn at mission conditions: Cotton fabric, Nomex (aramid), Nylon (hook-and-loop)
Apollo 13 (1970): medium match. High-pressure oxygen tanks with internal heaters/fans or valves
Mir (1997): medium match. Solid-fuel oxygen generators carried as backup

sections.title: What has not been tested
bullets: 12 of 96 condition cells have flight data.
Next experiment: Flammability of cabin materials at lunar gravity, 8.2 psia / 34% O2.
Parabolic flight at the target gravity (about 20 s per parabola) for ignition and early spread; sustained spread needs a rotating rig or surface tests.
Replaces interpolated limits for 3 ranked material(s) with measured ones.

sections.title: Recommendations
bullets: [P1] Re-screen soft goods at the mission atmosphere (approved)
[P2] Do not rely on fan shutdown alone (approved)
[P1] Detect smoke where the air goes, and sense gases too (approved)
[P2] Audit electrical parts inside oxygen tanks (approved)
[P1] Treat oxygen generators as ignition hazards (approved)
